paragraphs.source_en: “Kangetsu, the name of the lady who called out to you even in your dreams seemed to be a secret at the time. But surely you can tell us now.” Meitei began teasing Kangetsu. Kangetsu said, “If it were only a matter concerning myself, I should not mind telling you. But if I were to speak of it, it would cause trouble for the other party.” Meitei said, “So you still refuse to tell us, then.” Kangetsu said, “Besides, I have already given my word to the wife of a certain doctor.” Meitei said, “A promise not to tell anyone else?” “Yes.” As usual, Kangetsu began fingering the cord on his haori; it was a purple silk cord of a sort hardly ever seen for sale. “The color of that cord is rather behind the times.” The master said this while lying on his side. The master had not the slightest interest in the Kaneda affair. Meitei went on, “Quite so. In any case, it certainly is not something from the Russo-Japanese War period. Unless one wore a battle hat and a split-backed short haori bearing a pyramid-shaped hollyhock crest, a thing like that would never sit properly. They say that when Oda Nobunaga went to be married into another family, he wore his hair tied like a tea whisk; I imagine this is just the kind of cord he used to bind it at the root.” Meitei’s sentences were, as always, exceedingly long. Kangetsu answered with perfect seriousness, “To tell the truth, this is the cord my old father used during the Choshu campaign.” Meitei said, “You had better donate it to a museum, any old way. For the celebrated Mizushima Kangetsu, Bachelor of Science and lecturer on the mechanics of hanging, to appear dressed like an obsolete hatamoto samurai rather compromises his dignity.” Kangetsu said, “I could certainly throw it away, just as you advise. However, there is someone who tells me this cord suits me very well.” The master, still lying down, rolled over and said loudly, “Who could say anything so tasteless?” Kangetsu said, “It is someone you gentlemen do not know.” The master said, “It makes no difference whether we know her or not. Who is it?” Kangetsu answered, “A certain lady.” Meitei cut in from the side, “Ha, ha, ha. What a connoisseur she must be. Shall I guess? I daresay it is the woman who called your name from the bottom of the Sumida River. Why not put on that haori and make another splendid departure for the other world?” Kangetsu said, “Heh, heh. She no longer calls me from under the water, but from that pure world to the northwest...” Meitei said, “It may not be all that pure. That nose is positively terrifying.” “Who?” A look of surprise came over Kangetsu’s face. Meitei said, “The woman from the lane across the way turned up here just now. She gave the two of us quite a start, didn’t she, Kushami?” “Mm.” The master grunted and drank his tea while lying down. Kangetsu said, “Whose nose do you mean?” Meitei said, “Why, the honorable mother of your eternal woman.” “Oh!” Kangetsu cried out.

units.source_zh: 寒月说：“嘿嘿……她已经不再从水底呼唤我，而是从西北方的那个清净的世界……”迷亭说：“也未必怎样清净吧，那鼻子可是怪吓人的哩。”

units.source_en: “Who?”
A look of surprise came over Kangetsu’s face.
units.source_zh: 寒月脸上显出惊奇的神色。

units.source_en: Meitei said, “The woman from the lane across the way turned up here just now. She gave the two of us quite a start, didn’t she, Kushami?”
units.source_zh: 迷亭说：“对面那条胡同的女人，刚才在这儿露面啦，真让我们两个人大吃一惊，苦沙弥君，对吧？”

units.source_en: “Mm.”
The master grunted and drank his tea while lying down.
units.source_zh: 主人哼了一声，边卧着边喝茶。

units.source_en: Kangetsu said, “Whose nose do you mean?”
units.source_zh: 寒月说道：“您说的鼻子是指谁？”

units.source_en: Meitei said, “Why, the honorable mother of your eternal woman.”
units.source_zh: 迷亭说：“就是你那永远的女性的令堂大人呀。”

units.source_en: “Oh!”
Kangetsu cried out.
units.source_zh: 寒月叫了一声。

paragraphs.source_zh: “寒月君，那位在梦里都念叨你的妇人的名字，当时你好像还很保密。不过现在你总可以说了吧。”迷亭开始嘲弄起寒月来。寒月说：“如果只是我个人的事，即便对您说了也没有关系。可这事讲出来，会给对方带来麻烦呀。”迷亭说：“那么说，你还是不肯讲喽。”寒月说：“而且我已经对某某博士夫人作过保证了呢。”迷亭说：“是保证不对别人说吗？”“是的。”寒月和往常一样又在摆弄他那外褂上的穗子，那是个很少作为商品出售的紫色丝穗。“这丝穗的颜色未免有些落后于时代啊。”主人横躺着说。主人对金田事件毫不感兴趣。迷亭接着说：“就是嘛，这种丝穗毕竟不是当初日俄战争时代使用的东西。如果不是戴上‘阵笠’，穿上戴有金字塔形葵纹家徽的后开衩短外褂，挂上这种东西会显得不协调呢。据说织田信长去给人家做入赘女婿时，梳的是茶荃发，当时扎发根用的大概就是这种丝绳呢。”迷亭说的句子，总是那么老长老长。寒月一本正经地回答说：“说实话，这是老爷子在征伐长州时用的挂穗呢。”迷亭说：“我看你将它随便捐献给博物馆算了。一个演讲上吊力学的人，具有理学士头衔、鼎鼎大名的水岛寒月，居然打扮成早已过时的旗本武士模样，未免有失体统吧。”寒月说：“诚如尊谕，我未尝不可将它扔掉。不过，还有人对我说，这条挂穗对我很合适哩。”卧着的主人翻了个身，大声说：“是谁说出这样不懂行的话？”寒月说：“那可是你们所不认识的人。”主人说：“我们不认识也没关系，到底是谁呀？”寒月答道：“某位女性呗。”迷亭从旁接过话茬说：“哈哈……你也真够逗的，让我猜一猜好吗？恐怕就是从隅田川的水底下呼唤你名字的那个女人吧。你就干脆穿着这身外褂，再来一回驾返瑶池怎样？”寒月说：“嘿嘿……她已经不再从水底呼唤我，而是从西北方的那个清净的世界……”迷亭说：“也未必怎样清净吧，那鼻子可是怪吓人的哩。”“谁？”寒月脸上显出惊奇的神色。迷亭说：“对面那条胡同的女人，刚才在这儿露面啦，真让我们两个人大吃一惊，苦沙弥君，对吧？”“唔。”主人哼了一声，边卧着边喝茶。寒月说道：“您说的鼻子是指谁？”迷亭说：“就是你那永远的女性的令堂大人呀。”“唷！”寒月叫了一声。
